title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Science (086) · Crash revision of all assessed chapters (2026-27 syllabus)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written from this video's script, its worksheet and the NCERT/CBSE material it cites, modelled on most-repeated / high-weightage question types in CBSE Sample Question Papers and past board papers. instructions: 40 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number (negative allowed). No calculator.

patterns.T31: Power and current of an appliance

S1.name: Chemical Reactions and Equations
S1.tip: Balance with coefficients only, then name the type: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, redox. Oxidation = gain of O / loss of H.
S1.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 1: 'Types of chemical reactions' and 'Oxidation and reduction'; end-of-chapter exercises

S2.name: Acids, Bases and Salts
S2.tip: Learn each salt with its preparation equation and one use. Water of crystallisation: gypsum, PoP, washing soda, blue vitriol; baking soda has none. Enamel corrodes below pH 5.5.
S2.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 2: pH scale; 'More about salts' (NaOH, bleaching powder, baking soda, washing soda, PoP)

S3.name: Metals and Non-metals
S3.tip: Reactivity series K Na Ca Mg Al Zn Fe Pb [H] Cu Hg Ag Au decides displacement. Roasting = sulphide + excess air; calcination = carbonate + limited air. Al₂O₃ and ZnO are amphoteric.
S3.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 3: reactivity series, ionic compounds, extraction of metals, corrosion

S4.name: Carbon and its Compounds
S4.tip: Know CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ / CₙH₂ₙ / CₙH₂ₙ₋₂, the CH₂ (14 u) step, and the ethanol / ethanoic-acid reactions (oxidation, esterification, dehydration at 443 K). Soap + hard water → scum.
S4.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 4: homologous series, chemical properties of carbon compounds, ethanol and ethanoic acid, soaps and detergents

S5.name: Life Processes
S5.tip: Pyruvate → lactic acid (muscle, no O₂), ethanol + CO₂ (yeast), CO₂ + H₂O (mitochondria). Bile: alkaline + breaks fats into globules. Four chambers keep oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart.
S5.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 5: nutrition, respiration, transportation (heart), excretion (nephron)

S6.name: Control and Coordination
S6.tip: Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector. Medulla: involuntary actions. Touch-me-not: water movement, not growth. Pollen tube: chemotropism.
S6.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 6: reflex action, human brain, coordination in plants, hormones in animals

S7.name: How do Organisms Reproduce?
S7.tip: Match mode to organism: Amoeba fission, Plasmodium multiple fission, Hydra budding, Planaria regeneration, Spirogyra fragmentation, Rhizopus spores. Ovary → fruit, ovule → seed.
S7.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 7: modes of asexual reproduction; sexual reproduction in flowering plants; reproductive health

S8.name: Heredity
S8.tip: Monohybrid F₂ 3 : 1 (genotype 1 : 2 : 1); dihybrid F₂ 9 : 3 : 3 : 1. Multiply the fraction by the total. Father's X or Y decides the sex of the child.
S8.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 8: Mendel's contributions, inheritance of traits, sex determination

S9.name: Our Environment
S9.tip: About 10% of energy passes to the next trophic level, so multiply or divide by 10 per step. Pesticides concentrate most at the top level. O₂ → O + O (UV), O + O₂ → O₃.
S9.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 13: food chains and webs, ozone layer, waste management

S10.name: Light: Reflection and Refraction
S10.tip: Put signs in first (u is negative). Mirror 1/v + 1/u = 1/f, lens 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; lens m = v/u. P = 1/f with f in metres. n = c/v.
S10.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 9: mirror formula and magnification, refractive index, lens formula, power of a lens

S11.name: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
S11.tip: Myopia → concave lens; hypermetropia → convex lens. Violet deviates most, red least. Blue sky: fine particles scatter blue most; no atmosphere means a dark sky.
S11.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 10: defects of vision and their correction, dispersion by a prism, scattering of light

S12.name: Electricity
S12.tip: Series: add R, same current. Parallel: add 1/R, then invert, same voltage. P = VI = I²R = V²/R; H = I²Rt. A wire cut into n parts and joined in parallel becomes R/n².
S12.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 11: Ohm's law, resistivity, series and parallel resistors, heating effect, electric power

S13.name: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
S13.tip: Right-hand thumb rule for the field round a wire; Fleming's LEFT hand for the force (forefinger field, middle finger current, thumb motion). Field lines never cross. Earth wire protects metal bodies.
S13.ncert: NCERT Science Ch 12: field lines, field due to a current, force on a conductor, domestic electric circuits

questions.question: Which type of reaction is CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + heat?
questions.explanation: Two substances form one product and heat is released: an exothermic combination reaction.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: CuO loses oxygen to become Cu, so it is reduced; R is the definition that explains A.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: In the reaction CuO + H₂ → Cu + H₂O, copper oxide is reduced.
questions.reason: Reduction is the loss of oxygen (or gain of hydrogen) by a substance.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Water is electrolysed and 24 mL of hydrogen collects at the cathode. How many mL of oxygen collect at the anode in the same time?
questions.explanation: 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂: hydrogen and oxygen form in the ratio 2 : 1 by volume, so 24 ÷ 2 = 12 mL.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: Chemical Reactions and Equations; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In the chlor-alkali process, which gas is released at the anode?
questions.explanation: 2NaCl + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + Cl₂ + H₂: chlorine at the anode, hydrogen at the cathode, NaOH near the cathode.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Acids, Bases and Salts; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which set contains ONLY substances that have water of crystallisation?
questions.explanation: Gypsum CaSO₄·2H₂O, washing soda Na₂CO₃·10H₂O and PoP CaSO₄·½H₂O all have it; baking soda NaHCO₃ has none.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Acids, Bases and Salts; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Baking soda, common salt, Plaster of Paris
Gypsum, washing soda, Plaster of Paris

questions.question: Four solutions have pH P = 2, Q = 5, R = 7 and S = 12. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: Lower pH = more H⁺, so P is the strongest acid; S is basic (pink with phenolphthalein). pH 5 is below 5.5, so Q can corrode enamel; R is neutral.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Acids, Bases and Salts; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Q is safe for tooth enamel because it is close to neutral
S turns phenolphthalein pink, and P has the highest H⁺ ion concentration

questions.question: Which of these oxides reacts with both acids and bases?
questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide is amphoteric: Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O and Al₂O₃ + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO₂ + H₂O. Na₂O and CaO are basic, SO₂ is acidic.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Metals and Non-metals; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Heating zinc carbonate strongly in a limited supply of air is called:
questions.explanation: Calcination: carbonate ore in limited air, ZnCO₃ → ZnO + CO₂. Roasting is for sulphide ores in excess air.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Metals and Non-metals; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: A is false: ionic compounds conduct only when molten or dissolved. R is true and is exactly why solid NaCl does not conduct.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: Metals and Non-metals; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.reason: In the solid state, the ions of an ionic compound are held in place and cannot move.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: By how many units (u) does the molecular mass of butane, C₄H₁₀, exceed that of ethane, C₂H₆? (C = 12 u, H = 1 u)
questions.explanation: 58 − 30 = 28 u: they are two members apart in the alkane series, and each step adds CH₂ = 14 u.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Carbon and its Compounds; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Compound X (C₂H₄O₂) turns blue litmus red and, when warmed with ethanol and a few drops of concentrated sulphuric acid, gives a sweet-smelling substance. X is:
questions.explanation: An acid that forms a sweet-smelling ester with ethanol is ethanoic acid, CH₃COOH: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH → CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Carbon and its Compounds; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; the scum formation (R) is the reason soap fails to lather (A). Detergents still lather.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Carbon and its Compounds; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Soap does not lather well in hard water.
questions.reason: Calcium and magnesium ions in hard water react with soap to form an insoluble substance called scum.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: In human muscle cells during heavy exercise (shortage of oxygen), pyruvate is converted into:
questions.explanation: Without enough oxygen, muscle cells make lactic acid (causing cramps). Yeast makes ethanol + CO₂; mitochondria make CO₂ + water with oxygen.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Life Processes; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: What does bile from the liver do in the small intestine?
questions.explanation: Bile has no enzyme; it makes the medium alkaline for pancreatic enzymes and emulsifies fats.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Life Processes; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Makes the food alkaline and breaks fats into small globules

questions.question: Why do birds and mammals need a four-chambered heart with double circulation?
questions.explanation: Separation gives a highly efficient oxygen supply, which warm-blooded animals need. Fish have a two-chambered heart and single circulation.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: Life Processes; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It lets blood pass through the heart only once per cycle, as in fish
It keeps oxygenated and deoxygenated blood apart, giving the efficient oxygen supply needed to keep a constant body temperature
It mixes oxygenated and deoxygenated blood to save energy
It is needed only to pump blood to the lungs

questions.question: A pollen tube grows towards the ovule. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Growth in response to a chemical stimulus is chemotropism.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Control and Coordination; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which is the correct path of a reflex arc?
questions.explanation: The impulse goes in through the sensory neuron, the spinal cord responds, and the motor neuron carries it to the muscle or gland.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Control and Coordination; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Effector → motor neuron → spinal cord → sensory neuron → receptor
Receptor → spinal cord → sensory neuron → effector → motor neuron
Receptor → motor neuron → brain → sensory neuron → effector
Receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: A is false: no growth is involved. R is true: the leaves fold because water moves out of cells.
questions.remediation: Video part 6: Control and Coordination; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: The folding of touch-me-not leaves on touching is a growth movement.
questions.reason: The movement happens because the cells change their water content, which changes their shape.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Which organism is correctly matched with its mode of asexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Hydra buds; Planaria regenerates; Spirogyra fragments; Rhizopus forms spores.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: How do Organisms Reproduce?; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: After fertilisation in a flower, which change takes place?
questions.explanation: The ovary ripens into the fruit and each ovule develops into a seed; petals and sepals usually fall off.
questions.remediation: Video part 7: How do Organisms Reproduce?; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovule becomes the seed
The ovule becomes the fruit and the ovary becomes the seed

questions.question: In a dihybrid cross (round yellow × wrinkled green), 160 seeds are obtained in F₂. How many are expected to be wrinkled and yellow?
questions.explanation: F₂ ratio 9 : 3 : 3 : 1; wrinkled yellow is a '3' class: 3/16 × 160 = 30.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Heredity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In a monohybrid F₂ of 400 pea plants (from Tt × Tt), how many plants are expected to be tall AND pure-breeding (TT)?
questions.explanation: Genotypes are 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 1/4 of 400 = 100. Tall plants total 300, but only TT breed true.
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Heredity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and R explains A: the father's chromosome (X or Y) decides girl (XX) or boy (XY).
questions.remediation: Video part 8: Heredity; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: The sex of a child in humans is decided by the father.
questions.reason: The mother always gives an X chromosome, while the father gives either an X or a Y.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Producers in a food chain hold 20,000 kJ of energy. Using the 10% law, how many kJ reach the third trophic level?
questions.explanation: Level 1 → 2: 2,000 kJ; level 2 → 3: 200 kJ.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Our Environment; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In a food chain grass → grasshopper → frog → snake, a pesticide will be found in the highest concentration in:
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable chemicals build up at each level (biological magnification), so the top consumer has the most.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Our Environment; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: How is ozone formed in the upper atmosphere?
questions.explanation: O₂ → O + O (UV); O + O₂ → O₃. CFCs destroy ozone rather than form it.
questions.remediation: Video part 9: Our Environment; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: UV radiation splits O₂ into free O atoms, which combine with O₂ to form O₃
CFCs combine with oxygen to form O₃
Lightning combines nitrogen with oxygen to form O₃

questions.question: An object is placed 20 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. How far from the mirror (in cm) is the image formed?
questions.explanation: u = −20 cm, f = −10 cm. 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/10 + 1/20 = −1/20, so v = −20 cm: 20 cm in front (object at C, image at C).
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Light: Reflection and Refraction; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A 2 cm tall object is placed 30 cm in front of a convex lens of focal length 20 cm. Find the height of the image in cm, with its sign.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Light: Reflection and Refraction; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Find the power (in dioptres, with sign) of a concave lens of focal length 25 cm.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Light: Reflection and Refraction; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Light travels at 3 × 10⁸ m/s in air and 2 × 10⁸ m/s in a glass slab. The refractive index of the glass with respect to air is:
questions.explanation: n = speed in air ÷ speed in glass = 3 ÷ 2 = 1.5.
questions.remediation: Video part 10: Light: Reflection and Refraction; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A person cannot see distant objects clearly. The defect and its correcting lens are:
questions.explanation: Short-sightedness (myopia): the image forms in front of the retina; a diverging (concave) lens corrects it.
questions.remediation: Video part 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour bends the least?
questions.explanation: VIBGYOR: violet deviates most, red least.
questions.remediation: Video part 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and R explains A: the blue sky is due to scattering by fine particles in the atmosphere.
questions.remediation: Video part 11: The Human Eye and the Colourful World; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: To an astronaut far above the atmosphere, the sky looks dark instead of blue.
questions.reason: Without an atmosphere, there are no particles to scatter sunlight.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Resistors of 2 Ω, 4 Ω and 6 Ω are joined in series to a 24 V battery. What current (in A) flows?
questions.explanation: Rₛ = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12 Ω; I = V/R = 24/12 = 2 A (same through each).
questions.remediation: Video part 12: Electricity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A 6 Ω and a 3 Ω resistor are joined in parallel, and this combination is joined in series with a 4 Ω resistor. Find the total resistance in Ω.
questions.remediation: Video part 12: Electricity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A wire of resistance 27 Ω is cut into three equal parts, and the parts are joined in parallel. Find the resistance (in Ω) of the combination.
questions.explanation: Each part is 9 Ω (R ∝ l). Three 9 Ω in parallel: 9/3 = 3 Ω, i.e. R/9.
questions.remediation: Video part 12: Electricity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: An electric heater is rated 1100 W, 220 V. What current (in A) does it draw?
questions.remediation: Video part 12: Electricity; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the middle finger points in the direction of the:
questions.explanation: Forefinger: field; middle finger: current; thumb: force / motion of the conductor.
questions.remediation: Video part 13: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and R is the standard reason for A.
questions.remediation: Video part 13: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Two magnetic field lines never intersect each other.
questions.reason: If they crossed, a compass needle at that point would have to point in two directions at once, which is impossible.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Why is the metal body of an electric iron connected to the earth wire?
questions.explanation: The earth wire gives leakage current a low-resistance path to the earth, keeping the body at earth potential. The fuse is still needed for overloading and short circuits.
questions.remediation: Video part 13: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: So that the fuse is not needed
So that any leakage current flows to the earth and the user does not get a severe shock
So that the iron uses less power
So that the current through the element increases
